statement_record.intree: Local smallness is built into the definition of Category: hom X Y : Type@{h} is a fixed-universe type equipped with homset : Setoid (hom X Y), i.e. every category is Set(oid)-enriched and hence locally small by construction.  The phrase 'locally small' is used in the hom-functor / representable-functor headers.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger-by-fiat: whereas Awodey makes local smallness a DISTINGUISHING property (some categories have it, some do not), the library only ever constructs locally-small categories -- the homset field forces every category to have genuine hom-sets at a fixed universe level h.  The concept 'hom-set' is thus definitionally present and universal, but as a classifying definition it is vacuous here (a non-locally-small category cannot even be expressed).
